docs.title: Elysia E-Commerce API
docs.text: A production-oriented e-commerce backend built with Elysia.js, Bun, Drizzle ORM, and PostgreSQL.

docs.title: What is included
docs.text:
• Checkout that handles reality

    Guest carts, variant-level pricing and stock, checkout quotes, idempotent order creation, payment windows, order timelines, and guest order tokens.

  • Catalog & discovery

    Brands, category trees, slugs/SEO metadata, facets, related products, review images, product Q&A, multi-currency display, translations, and full-text search with typo tolerance.

  • Post-purchase

    Regional tax rates, country-aware shipping/free-shipping rules, returns/RMA with stock restoration, refunds, and printable invoices.

  • Payments & messaging

    Provider adapter, signed/idempotent webhooks, saved tokenized methods, notification preferences, and a retried transactional email outbox.

  • Marketplace operations

    Seller fulfillment, commission/payout tracking, coupon scopes and stacking, gift cards, sales reports, and audit logs.

  • Security & platform

    TOTP 2FA with recovery codes, scoped API keys, GDPR export/deletion, /api/v1 aliases, Prometheus metrics, and health checks.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/piashcse/elysia-ecommerce.git
cd elysia-ecommerce
bun install
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env with your database credentials
bun run db:migrate
bun run dev
  • API: http://localhost:3000
  • Swagger UI: http://localhost:3000/swagger
  • OpenAPI JSON: http://localhost:3000/swagger/json

docs.title: Base URL & versioning
docs.text:
Every route is available under the stable /api/v1 prefix:

http://localhost:3000/api/v1/products/

The unversioned equivalents (/products/, /orders/, …) remain available for backwards compatibility. New integrations should use /api/v1.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The application is a modular monolith designed around clear service boundaries. Controllers only translate HTTP requests and responses; business rules live in services; Drizzle ORM owns persistence.

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
Request
  → request ID + security headers + CORS
  → rate limiter
  → auth plugin (JWT or API key, loads the live user)
  → route validation (TypeBox)
  → controller
  → service / database transaction
  → response envelope + sanitization
  → logging / audit middleware
Response

Key files:

File Responsibility src/server.ts App composition, middleware, error handler, OpenAPI src/core/auth.ts JWT/API-key authentication and role macros src/core/responses.ts Success/paginated/error envelopes and sanitization src/config/database.ts PostgreSQL pool and Drizzle client src/core/base.service.ts Shared find/create/update primitives src/database/schema/ Drizzle table definitions and indexes drizzle/ Tracked SQL migrations and metadata

docs.title: Data & migrations
docs.text:
• Schema definitions live in src/database/schema/.
  • Migrations are generated with bun run db:generate and applied with bun run db:migrate.
  • The catalog search migration enables the PostgreSQL pg_trgm extension and creates full-text/trigram GIN indexes.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: Checkout, stock changes, coupon usage, gift-card redemption, and payment records run inside database transactions. Stock updates use conditional UPDATE … WHERE stock >= quantity statements so concurrent checkouts cannot oversell inventory.

docs.title: Background work
docs.text:
• Email outbox — transactional emails are persisted first, then delivered by POST /emails/process or the in-process worker (EMAIL_WORKER_ENABLED=true). Failed attempts use exponential backoff.
  • Expired orders — call POST /orders/release-expired from your scheduler to cancel unpaid orders, restore stock, release coupons, and restore gift-card balances.

docs.title: External integrations
docs.text:
The codebase ships adapter boundaries rather than hard dependencies:

Concern Current implementation Payments Simulated provider + signed webhook contract Email Dev logging + optional MAIL_WEBHOOK_URL transport Media Local uploads/ directory served by the API Search PostgreSQL full-text + trigram (no external engine required) Shipping rates Configured shipping methods and country rules

docs.title: Currencies
docs.text:
Exchange rates are stored in the currencies table as 1 USD = rate units of the target currency. USD is seeded by the migration with a rate of 1.

  • GET /api/v1/currencies lists active currencies.
  • GET /api/v1/currencies/convert?amount=10&from=USD&to=EUR converts an amount.
  • Admin routes create/update/deactivate currencies.
  • Orders and quotes accept a currency field and persist the applied rate.
  • Catalog endpoints accept ?currency=EUR for display conversion.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
The catalog search migration requires the pg_trgm extension. The migration runs CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm. If your database user cannot create extensions, enable it once as a superuser:

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Use a random JWT_SECRET of at least 32 characters in production.
  • Set PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET to a provider-issued secret and rotate it.
  • Restrict ALLOWED_ORIGINS to trusted frontends.
  • API keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes; the plaintext key is returned only once.
  • 2FA recovery codes are single-use and stored as hashes.

Tests run against TEST_DB_NAME (default elysia_ecom_test). The test helper creates the database, applies migrations, and truncates tables between runs.

Test files live in src/tests/ and exercise the HTTP API through app.handle(), so they cover routing, validation, auth, and persistence.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The docs site uses MkDocs Material.

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

# 1. Refresh the OpenAPI snapshot (server must be running)
bun run docs:snapshot

# 2. Regenerate the Markdown API reference
bun run docs:generate

# 3. Preview
bun run docs:serve

# 4. Build exactly like CI
bun run docs:build

Publishing helpers:

Command Description bun run docs:fix-pages Point GitHub Pages at gh-pages and queue a build bun run docs:build Build with mkdocs build --strict

docs/openapi.json is committed so the GitHub Pages workflow can build the site without a database or running server. Regenerate the snapshot whenever a route or request/response schema changes.

Generated files:

  • docs/<module>.md — one page per OpenAPI tag
  • docs/api-reference/index.md — endpoint index grouped by module

Overview and guide pages (index.md, architecture.md, configuration.md, errors.md, development.md, changelog.md) are maintained by hand.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the site with mkdocs build --strict and deploys it to the gh-pages branch using mkdocs gh-deploy. The workflow runs on pushes to main that touch docs-related files, and can be triggered manually.

One-time repository setup:

  1. Push the repository to GitHub.
  2. Run bun run docs:fix-pages (requires gh auth login), or open Settings → Pages and set Source to Deploy from a branch → gh-pages → / (root).
  3. The docs workflow creates/updates gh-pages and queues a Pages build.

If the site shows only the README

This means GitHub Pages is still serving the main branch root, not the built MkDocs site. Run bun run docs:fix-pages, or change Settings → Pages → Source to Deploy from a branch → gh-pages → / (root).

main / (root) uses Jekyll and renders README.md; it does not serve the MkDocs output. The docs.yml workflow deploys the MkDocs site to the gh-pages branch with mkdocs gh-deploy.

Because pushes made with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger a Pages build, the workflow explicitly requests a build after deploying. It also fails with the exact gh api command if the Pages source is not gh-pages.
